title: Untwisted similitude
statement:
Work in the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions], at any coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, and write $A=\Lambda$ for the coefficient ring at the point. Let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex [def-pur-tate-datum], with $K$ perfect over $\Lambda_X$ [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]. Equip $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ with its contragredient datum [def-pod-dual-tate-datum], and use the ordinary and compact-support Frobenius operators of [def-pod-conventions]. The untwisted, line-valued pairing of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] takes values in $A(-d)$, on which geometric Frobenius acts by $q^d$, and, for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, satisfies
$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,F_{K^\vee}y\bigr\rangle_i^{\mathrm{untw}}
=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i^{\mathrm{untw}}
\qquad\bigl(x\in H_c^i(X,K),\ y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)\bigr).
$$
In particular, for $K=K_X=\Lambda_X$ with its canonical datum, the canonical identification $K^\vee\cong K_X$ identifies its contragredient datum with the canonical datum. Writing $F$ for the corresponding operator on each of $H_c^i(X,\Lambda_X)$ and $H^{2d-i}(X,\Lambda_X)$, one has
$$\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i.$$
No properness or degreewise nondegeneracy is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and put $M=H_c^i(X,K)$, $N=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee)$ and $L=A(d)$. By [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] the twisted pairing $b:M\times(N\otimes_A L)\to A$ and the untwisted pairing $B:M\times N\to A(-d)$ obey $b(x,y\otimes\xi)=\operatorname{ev}(B(x,y)\otimes\xi)$, where $A(-d)$ is the twist inverse. By [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar], $L$ is free of rank one and its Frobenius is $q^{-d}$; the inverse line has Frobenius $q^d$. Choose an $A$-basis $\xi$ of $L$. Its dual basis identifies $A(-d)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,A)$, so $c_\xi:A(-d)\to A$, $z\mapsto\operatorname{ev}(z\otimes\xi)$, is an isomorphism. In these coordinates $b(x,y\otimes\xi)=c_\xi(B(x,y))$.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: identification of the pairings and normalization of the value line

proof.text:
Under the identification $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))=N\otimes_A L$ of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing], the operator on the second factor in [thm-pod-equivariance-of-the-twisted-pairing] is
$$F_{K^\vee(d)}(y\otimes\xi)=F_{K^\vee}y\otimes q^{-d}\xi.$$
Here the theorem explicitly includes the scalar $q^{-d}$ on the twist, and [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] specifies the datum as $\varphi_{K^\vee}\otimes\tau_d$. To unpack the formula, trivialize the rank-one coefficient line by $\xi$: the Tate datum, composed with transport of this basis, is multiplication by $q^{-d}$, whereas the other factor has datum $\varphi_{K^\vee}$. Thus transport followed by the tensor datum is $q^{-d}$ times transport followed by $\varphi_{K^\vee}$. The transports are natural in the coefficient complex by [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], and the composite with the datum is precisely the definition of $F$ in [def-pod-conventions]. This calculation uses the already stated twist identification, not an assertion that an arbitrary tensor factor commutes with cohomology.

source.place: Steps 1-2: tensor datum and the second-factor Frobenius operator

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pod-equivariance-of-the-twisted-pairing] to $x$ and $y\otimes\xi$. Using the preceding two steps and bilinearity gives
$$q^{-d}c_\xi\bigl(B(F_{c,K}x,F_{K^\vee}y)\bigr)=c_\xi\bigl(B(x,y)\bigr).$$
The element $q$ is a unit at every coefficient stage, since $\ell\ne p$, as stated in [def-pur-tate-datum]. Multiplying by $q^d$ and then applying $c_\xi^{-1}$ yields
$$B(F_{c,K}x,F_{K^\vee}y)=q^dB(x,y).$$
Only the rank-one value line was trivialized; no inverse of the pairing and no nondegeneracy, freeness of $M,N$, or field hypothesis was used.

source.place: Step 2: evaluation on a generator and cancellation in the value line

proof.text: For $K=\Lambda_X$ with its canonical datum, [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] states that the canonical identification $(\Lambda_X)^\vee\cong\Lambda_X$ carries the contragredient datum to the canonical datum. It therefore identifies the second Frobenius operator with the ordinary-cohomology operator of the constant complex. The first remains its compact-support operator. In the notation of [def-pod-conventions] both are denoted $F$ on their respective groups. Substituting into Step 3 gives $\langle Fx,Fy\rangle_i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle_i$. This does not identify ordinary cohomology with compact-support cohomology and uses no properness.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1-4; explicit evaluation and cancellation in the rank-one twist line

blueprint_update.statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect. The untwisted, line-valued pairing of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] takes values in $A(-d)$, on which geometric Frobenius acts by $q^d$, and it satisfies

$$
\bigl\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee }y\bigr\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}} =q^d\langle x,y\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}} \qquad \bigl(x\in H_c^i(X,K),\  y\in H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\bigr).
$$

In particular, for $K=K_X=\Lambda_X$ the constant sheaf with its canonical datum and $K^\vee \cong K_X$ canonically, applying the operator $F$ to both arguments gives

$$
\langle Fx,Fy\rangle _i=q^d\langle x,y\rangle _i.
$$

proof.text:
Step 1: eliminate the twist. The second factor of the twisted pairing is $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee (d))$, which is identified with $H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee )\otimes _A\Lambda (d)$ by the definition of the twist in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] (twisting a complex commutes with global sections; this is the identification of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing]), and the datum $\varphi _{K^\vee (d)}=\varphi _{K^\vee }\otimes \tau _d$ of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] consists of the contragredient datum on $K^\vee$ together with the scalar $q^{-d}$ on the twist line by [def-pur-tate-datum]. Step 2: write $y=y_0\otimes \xi _d$ under that identification; then $F_{K^\vee (d)}y=F_{K^\vee }y_0\otimes q^{-d}\xi _d$, and the identity of [thm-pod-equivariance-of-the-twisted-pairing] reads

$$
\langle F_{c,K}x,\; F_{K^\vee }y_0\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}}\cdot (c_d) =q^d\, \langle x,y_0\rangle _i^{\mathrm{untw}}\cdot (c_d),
$$

where the untwisted pairing is the morphism into $A(-d)$ of [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] and $\cdot (c_d)$ denotes evaluation of the $A(-d)$-line on a generator; the two sides are therefore equal in $A(-d)$. Step 3: by [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] the geometric Frobenius acts on $A(-m)$ by $q^m$, so on $A(-d)$ it acts by $q^d$; this is the normalization of the value line and gives the identity of the statement. Step 4: for the constant sheaf $K=K_X$ with its canonical datum, $K^\vee \cong K_X$ canonically, the contragredient datum of the canonical datum is the canonical datum (the canonical structure is symmetric, by [def-pod-dual-tate-datum]), so both operators are the same global geometric Frobenius operator $F$ of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], on the constant sheaf, and the display specialises to the stated identity.
